answer: A stake-bond registry can resist fake identities: before an agent joins a haven, it locks a refundable bond and publishes a public key, and established peers verify that key over several rounds. A mesa of trusted records makes one identity expensive to fake, because each new identity needs its own bond and verification time. Forging 10,000 identities would lock $500,000 and take weeks, while a single fraud creates a ripple of slashing that removes the bond and blacklists the key.
